review_output: {"summary":"MAJOR1 is resolved, judged from the supplied source. The audit guard takes FOR SHARE on the version row. That lock conflicts with the FOR UPDATE taken first by create, claim and finish, so the lock order (version, then report) is the same everywhere. If an audit commits first, a new report is created afterwards and its snapshot sees the audit. If a create or claim commits first, the AFTER trigger's UPDATE runs in a fresh read-committed statement snapshot, sees that report and marks it stale. A worker whose snapshot predates the audit then gets 0 rows from finish, because finish only updates reports that are still running. MAJOR2 is resolved at the trigger level but not fully verified. wp20_metric_version_update raises sourceRevision on every UPDATE and makes collectionStartedAt immutable once set, so disable and re-enable each raise the revision. The report guard rejects running and ready reports that carry an old revision. Two things were not supplied: the coverage reader, which is where audits would be tied to the current revision, and the body of wp20_metric_report_invalidate. Re-enable also has no test yet. MAJOR3 is partly resolved: all four kinds are read under one shared budget in a single RepeatableRead snapshot. It stays open because no calculator adapter or producer is connected. This review does not certify the full WP or the producer. As instructed, I did not treat collection gaps after re-enable as a DB defect; they remain the producer's open responsibility.","findings":[{"file":"src/lib/live-metric-report-snapshot.ts","area":"per-kind coverage/evidence consistency","issue":"Order coverage is read in the snapshot, but no order rows are loaded in the same transaction.","evidence":"coverage(\"orders\") fills orderCoverage. MetricViewingSnapshot has no orders field and no order page loop.","impact":"If the calculator reads orders in a different transaction, a covered order certificate and the order rows it covers can come from different snapshots. A late order or audit could then be missed without anyone noticing.","recommended_fix":"Load order evidence in this same RepeatableRead transaction under the shared budget, or remove orderCoverage until order evidence is loaded here.","required_test":"Insert an order and its overlapping audit between two snapshot pages. Make coverage-unavailable propagate as unavailable, never as zero.","required_test":"End-to-end tests where each kind's coverage is unavailable, a gap, or a loss each give an unavailable metric for that kind only.","severity":"high","confidence":0.9},{"file":"prisma/migrations/20261015120000_live_metric_coverage_audit/migration.sql","area":"disable/re-enable revision binding","issue":"Rejecting old certificates after re-enable depends on the reader matching audit.sourceRevision to the current revision. Only the disable case was tested.","impact":"If the reader accepts audits with an older revision (<= current), a certificate from before the disable would still count after re-enable.","recommended_fix":"Make the reader require audit.sourceRevision = the current version revision, read in the same snapshot.","required_test":"Covered audit at revision N, then disable, then re-enable (revision N+2).
